title: Voevodsky motives and motives with modulus in positive characteristic: every proper interior generically finite h-covering is refined by a modulus qfh covering
author: Keiho Matsumoto
work: Voevodsky motives and motives with modulus in positive characteristic
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Proposition (source0.tex lines 603--621, source label hisqfh), the h-descent step on which the article's compact generation theorem for the triangulated category of motives with modulus rests: for any proper interior generically finite h-covering of a modulus pair, there exist a modulus pair M-prime, a minimal morphism b into the base, a finite Zariski family of modulus pairs U-prime-y and a family of coverings W-y to V-y to U-prime-y to M-prime which is again an interior generically finite h-covering, refines the given family in the category of modulus schemes, and fits into the stated commutative diagram with each comparison morphism in the class of minimal morphisms; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 623--707 (one adjacent proof environment of 85 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span together with the retained statement of the article's single-covering lemma. It chooses a finite set of points whose open neighbourhoods cover the interior, defines the closures Z-y of the complements and their intersection W, shows that W meets no interior point and has codimension at least two, blows up W, verifies that the strict transforms become disjoint with empty intersection so that the pulled-back open sets cover the blown-up model while restricting isomorphically to the original open sets, replaces the covering by a Zariski covering of modulus pairs, and applies the retained single-covering lemma to each member to produce the finite coverings and the minimal comparison morphisms, concluding that the resulting family is the required interior generically finite h-covering with the stated diagram. The upshot is an original research-level descent theorem of the theory of motives with modulus in positive characteristic, proved without resolution of singularities and using only a single covering lemma. H2: a research-level algebraic-geometry proposition whose proof combines a codimension count, a blow-up construction, strict-transform bookkeeping, Zariski descent of modulus pairs and a minimality argument, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
